newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says to buy back 50 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says to buy back 50 mln shares.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Friday it planned a 50 million share buyback from May 19.
Westpac said the on-market buyback of 2.8 percent of its issued capital would run for six months until November 18.

The bank said the new scheme in effect extended a buyback scheme announced in November 1996, but which could not be completed on time because repurchasing was suspended during negotiations with the Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
Westpac last November announced a buyback of up to five percent of its stock, or about 85 million shares, through to May.

"The extension of the buyback is consistent with our policy of active capital management and preserves the flexibility to respond to the creation of excess capital that may arise from the proposed merger with the Bank of Melbourne," chief financial officer Pat Handley said in a statement.
Westpac said it would not repurchase shares before May 19 due to the announcement of its half-year earnings on May 14.
Ord Minnett Securities Ltd and SBC Warburg Australia Equities Ltd would continue to act on its behalf in the buyback.
Westpac launched a A$1.435 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne on April 3.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has said it would rule on the takeover by early May.
